title: Climate Risk Stress Testing in California: A Geospatial Framework for Banking and Climate-Exposed Sectors
summary: This paper presents a geospatial framework for climate risk stress testing in California, integrating physical hazard mapping, sector-specific exposure analysis, and scenario-based financial risk assessment for banking and climate-exposed sectors (agriculture, real estate, tourism) against wildfires, drought, flooding, extreme heat, and transition risks. It includes a survey-based implementation guide for benchmarking climate-risk practices.
key_points: Focuses on physical climate risks: wildfires, drought, flooding, extreme heat, and transition risks affecting California
Applies geospatial framework to banking sector and climate-exposed sectors: agriculture, real estate, tourism
Integrates physical hazard mapping with sector-specific exposure and scenario-based financial risk assessment
Intended to support portfolio monitoring, climate scenario analysis, and institutional readiness under disclosure standards
Authors: Satya Narayana Panda and Aishworzo Saha
Includes a survey-based implementation guide for benchmarking current industry practices
why_it_matters: This research provides a methodological framework for assessing how physical climate risks translate into financial losses for banks and climate-exposed sectors. While not a macro catalyst in the traditional sense (no rate decision, economic data, or policy announcement), it contributes to climate risk analysis tooling that could influence how financial institutions stress-test portfolios under climate scenarios.
